assumptions: assumes the most recent value is the best available estimate of near-future values
assumes no reliable trend or seasonal signal
description: Repeats the last observed value for every future step (random walk without drift).
failure_conditions: degrades sharply when the series has a persistent trend
ignores seasonality entirely and fails on strongly seasonal series

assumptions: assumes the series is stationary around a constant mean
description: Forecasts every future step as the historical mean of the series.
failure_conditions: fails on trending series
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: assumes the average historical rate of change continues unchanged
requires at least 2 observations
description: Extrapolates a straight line from the first to the last observed value (random walk with drift).
failure_conditions: fails when the trend reverses direction after the observed window
amplifies noise from a volatile first or last observation

assumptions: requires a known seasonal_period and at least one full cycle of history
assumes the seasonal pattern is stable
description: Repeats the value observed one full seasonal cycle ago for each future step.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than one seasonal cycle
fails on series without genuine periodicity
ignores any trend

assumptions: assumes local stationarity over the averaging window
requires history length >= window size
description: Forecasts every future step as the mean of the last k observed values.
failure_conditions: lags behind trends by roughly half the window width
fails when history is shorter than the window

assumptions: assumes no trend and no seasonality
assumes an optimal smoothing parameter can be fit from history
description: Simple exponential smoothing; forecasts a flat line at the smoothed level, weighting recent observations more heavily.
failure_conditions: systematically under- or over-shoots trending series
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: assumes an approximately linear trend with no seasonality
description: Holt's linear (double) exponential smoothing; extrapolates a smoothed level and trend.
failure_conditions: over-extrapolates trend on long horizons
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: assumes a trend that weakens over time rather than continuing linearly
description: Holt's linear trend with a damping parameter that flattens the trend over the forecast horizon.
failure_conditions: under-forecasts series with a genuinely persistent linear trend
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes seasonal amplitude is roughly constant in absolute terms
description: Holt-Winters triple exponential smoothing with additive seasonality.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
misfits series where seasonal amplitude scales with the level

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
requires strictly positive values
assumes seasonal amplitude scales with the level
description: Holt-Winters triple exponential smoothing with multiplicative seasonality.
failure_conditions: undefined or unstable for series containing zero or negative values
fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes trend weakens over the forecast horizon
description: Holt-Winters triple exponential smoothing with a damped trend component.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
under-forecasts series with a persistent linear trend

assumptions: assumes one of the standard ETS error-trend-season combinations reasonably fits the series
description: Automatic selection among the additive/multiplicative/damped error-trend-season exponential smoothing state-space models by in-sample information criterion.
failure_conditions: selection can overfit short histories
multiplicative variants require strictly positive values

assumptions: assumes the series is well described by a linear trend and a locally weighted SES component
description: Classical Theta method; decomposes the series into long-term trend and local-curvature theta-lines and recombines their forecasts.
failure_conditions: fails on strongly seasonal series without prior deseasonalization
degrades on very short histories

assumptions: assumes the classical Theta method's structure holds but with data-driven parameters
description: Dynamic optimized Theta method; fits theta-line weights and smoothing parameters from history instead of using fixed defaults.
failure_conditions: can overfit very short histories
fails on strongly seasonal series without prior deseasonalization

assumptions: assumes the (differenced) series is stationary
assumes a linear autoregressive relationship
description: Autoregressive model; forecasts each value as a linear combination of a fitted number of past values.
failure_conditions: fails on non-stationary series without differencing
fails on series dominated by seasonality

assumptions: assumes the (differenced) series is stationary
assumes shocks have a linear, short-memory effect
description: Moving-average model; forecasts each value as a linear combination of past forecast errors.
failure_conditions: fails on non-stationary series without differencing
forecasts revert to the mean quickly and undershoot persistent trends

assumptions: assumes the series is stationary
assumes no seasonality
description: Combined autoregressive moving-average model.
failure_conditions: fails on non-stationary or seasonal series without preprocessing

assumptions: assumes differencing to a low order achieves stationarity
assumes no seasonality
description: Non-seasonal ARIMA with automatic (p, d, q) order selection by information criterion.
failure_conditions: order search can overfit short histories
fails on strongly seasonal series

assumptions: requires a known seasonal_period
requires enough history to estimate seasonal differencing reliably (multiple full cycles)
description: Seasonal ARIMA with automatic (p, d, q)(P, D, Q, m) order selection by information criterion.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than a few seasonal cycles
order search can be unstable on noisy series

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes the seasonal component is stable
description: STL-decomposes the series into trend, season, and remainder, extrapolates trend with a naive/drift method, and reapplies the last seasonal cycle.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
ignores structure in the remainder component

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes a fixed, non-evolving seasonal pattern
description: Classical additive/multiplicative decomposition into trend, season, and remainder, recombined with a simple trend extrapolation.
failure_conditions: moving-average trend estimate loses the most recent seasonal cycles at the series edges
fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
description: STL-decomposes the series, forecasts the seasonally adjusted series with ETS, and reapplies the seasonal component.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
compounds any ETS misfit from the decomposition step

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes the seasonally adjusted series is well modeled by ARIMA
description: STL-decomposes the series, forecasts the seasonally adjusted series with ARIMA, and reapplies the seasonal component.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
compounds any ARIMA misfit from the decomposition step

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent with a meaningful fraction of exact zeros
description: Croston's method; separately smooths non-zero demand sizes and inter-demand intervals for sparse/intermittent series.
failure_conditions: produces a biased (upward) forecast, a known property of standard Croston
degrades on dense, non-intermittent series

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent with a meaningful fraction of exact zeros
description: Croston's method with the Syntetos-Boylan Approximation bias correction applied to the demand-size/interval smoothing.
failure_conditions: still assumes a stable demand-generating process
degrades on dense, non-intermittent series

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent with a meaningful fraction of exact zeros
description: Teunter-Syntetos-Babai method; smooths demand probability and size separately, allowing the forecast to decay during long zero runs.
failure_conditions: degrades on dense, non-intermittent series
sensitive to the choice of smoothing parameters on short histories

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent
requires enough history to support the chosen aggregation level
description: Aggregate-Disaggregate Intermittent Demand Approach; temporally aggregates the series to a lower-intermittence frequency, forecasts, then disaggregates.
failure_conditions: fails when history is too short for the aggregation level chosen
disaggregation can misallocate volume within an aggregated period

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent
requires enough history to support multiple aggregation levels
description: Multiple Aggregation Prediction Algorithm; combines forecasts across several temporal aggregation levels of an intermittent series.
failure_conditions: fails when history is too short for the coarsest aggregation level
more computationally expensive than single-level ADIDA for uncertain benefit

assumptions: assumes no trend or seasonality, only a slowly drifting level plus noise
description: State-space local level (random walk plus noise) model estimated via the Kalman filter.
failure_conditions: fails on trending or seasonal series
underperforms simple naive methods when the level is actually constant

assumptions: assumes no seasonality, only a slowly evolving level and trend
description: State-space local linear trend model (stochastic level and slope) estimated via the Kalman filter.
failure_conditions: fails on seasonal series
can produce unstable long-horizon trend extrapolation if slope variance is large

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history to estimate the seasonal state
description: Basic structural model combining stochastic level, trend, and seasonal components in a single state-space model.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
estimation can be unstable on short or noisy series

assumptions: assumes the underlying trend is smooth and outliers are a minority of points
description: Extrapolates a robust locally weighted (LOESS) trend fit, downweighting outliers.
failure_conditions: ignores seasonality entirely
extrapolation beyond the fitted window is unstable for highly nonlinear local trends

assumptions: assumes a small number of dominant, stable periodic frequencies
requires a known or estimable seasonal_period
description: Regresses the series on a trend plus a fixed set of Fourier (sine/cosine) terms and extrapolates.
failure_conditions: fails on series with evolving or non-stationary periodicity
underfits series with sharp, non-sinusoidal seasonal shape

assumptions: assumes the trend is approximately linear
assumes no seasonality
description: Ordinary least squares regression of the series on a linear time index, extrapolated forward.
failure_conditions: fails on seasonal or nonlinear-trend series
sensitive to outliers near the end of history

assumptions: assumes the trend is well approximated by a low-order polynomial
assumes no seasonality
description: Least squares regression of the series on a low-order polynomial time index, extrapolated forward.
failure_conditions: extrapolation diverges quickly on longer horizons for polynomial order above 1
overfits short histories at higher polynomial orders

assumptions: assumes trend changes are sparse and detectable from history alone
assumes no seasonality
description: Fits a piecewise linear trend with one or more detected changepoints and extrapolates the final segment.
failure_conditions: changepoint detection is unreliable on short or noisy histories
extrapolating the final segment assumes no imminent further change

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes blocks of history are representative of future dynamics
description: Generates a forecast by block-bootstrapping historical seasonal-cycle-length blocks of the detrended series and averaging simulated paths.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
point forecast can be a poorly representative average when the simulated paths are multimodal

assumptions: assumes the three component methods have roughly independent errors so averaging reduces variance
description: Averages the point forecasts of ets_auto, arima_auto, and theta_optimized.
failure_conditions: inherits any failure shared by all three components, e.g. all three fail on a very short or heavily intermittent series
requires all three component methods to be available

assumptions: Past states close in lag space have similar future continuations.
description: Match the latest lag vector to historical lag vectors and average their observed continuations.
failure_conditions: Sparse history or a regime shift leaves no genuinely comparable analogue.

assumptions: Shape-similar episodes remain predictive despite local timing distortions.
description: Find historical subsequences with similar shape under dynamic time warping and aggregate their following paths.
failure_conditions: A permissive warping window can match unrelated episodes and erase timing information.

assumptions: Calibration and forecast residuals are sufficiently exchangeable over the evaluation period.
description: Calibrate forecast intervals with held-out absolute residual quantiles from a fixed point forecaster.
failure_conditions: Abrupt distribution shifts invalidate residual coverage learned from the calibration window.

assumptions: Coverage drift is gradual enough for online score updates to track it.
description: Update conformal interval widths online so recent coverage errors change the next interval.
failure_conditions: Fast alternating regimes cause the adaptation rule to lag or oscillate.

assumptions: Conditional count variance is close to the conditional mean after included predictors.
description: Model a count target with a log-linked Poisson mean driven by time and optional predictors.
failure_conditions: Strong overdispersion, zero inflation, or dependence left in residuals biases uncertainty.

assumptions: A negative-binomial conditional law captures extra-Poisson dispersion.
description: Forecast overdispersed counts with a dynamic negative-binomial regression mean.
failure_conditions: Structural zeros or changing dispersion violate the fitted conditional distribution.

assumptions: Count dependence can be represented by stable thinning probabilities and innovations.
description: Use binomial thinning of past integer counts plus an integer-valued innovation process.
failure_conditions: Nonlinear regime changes or strong covariate effects are not represented by a fixed INAR law.

assumptions: The chosen kernel expresses the smoothness and similarity structure of the lag-response map.
description: Place a Gaussian-process prior over the nonlinear mapping from lag vectors to future values.
failure_conditions: Poor kernels extrapolate badly and exact inference scales cubically with training cases.

assumptions: A fixed kernel can represent the stable nonlinear relationship between features and target.
description: Fit epsilon-insensitive support-vector regression to lag and calendar features and roll it forward.
failure_conditions: Recursive multi-step use compounds error and kernel tuning can be unstable on short series.

assumptions: Future responses vary smoothly under the selected kernel geometry.
description: Apply ridge-regularized kernel regression to lagged and optional exogenous features.
failure_conditions: Kernel matrices become costly on large samples and extrapolation beyond observed features is weak.

assumptions: A stable nonlinear lag relationship can be learned from enough repeated patterns.
description: Feed lagged observations and seasonal lags to a shallow multilayer perceptron and recursively forecast.
failure_conditions: Small samples, regime shifts, and recursive error accumulation degrade long-horizon forecasts.

assumptions: Related training series share learnable dynamics and the chosen likelihood is suitable.
description: Train one autoregressive recurrent network across related series to output a parametric predictive distribution.
failure_conditions: Few unrelated series or a misspecified likelihood prevent useful global transfer.

assumptions: A large collection of training windows supports learning reusable basis expansions.
description: Stack backward and forward fully connected residual blocks with optional trend and seasonal bases.
failure_conditions: Very small samples or abrupt unseen regimes cause high-variance extrapolation.

assumptions: Forecast structure can be decomposed across multiple temporal resolutions.
description: Use hierarchical interpolation and multi-rate input pooling to model different forecast frequencies.
failure_conditions: Resolution choices can suppress sharp high-frequency events important to the target.

assumptions: Known-future and observed covariates contain stable cross-series predictive information.
description: Combine recurrent local processing, variable selection, gating, and attention for multi-horizon forecasts with covariates.
failure_conditions: Sparse data or unreliable future covariates make the high-capacity architecture overfit.

assumptions: Outlier timing or intervention shape can be identified separately from recurring dynamics.
description: Jointly estimate ARIMA dynamics and explicit pulse, level-shift, or temporary-change intervention effects.
failure_conditions: Many overlapping anomalies are confounded with structural breaks and ARIMA parameters.

assumptions: A sparse set of abnormal observations contaminates an otherwise stable ARIMA process.
description: Detect additive and innovative outliers, estimate their effects, clean the series, and refit ARIMA.
failure_conditions: Persistent regime changes are incorrectly removed as isolated contamination.

assumptions: A small set of persistent latent regimes generates the observed dynamics.
description: Use a latent Markov state to switch autoregressive parameters, level, or variance across regimes.
failure_conditions: Regimes with few visits are weakly identified and unprecedented states cannot be represented.

assumptions: Regime transitions are driven by observable threshold conditions.
description: Switch autoregressive equations when a threshold variable crosses estimated cut points.
failure_conditions: Smooth transitions or time-varying thresholds make hard partitions unstable.

assumptions: Nonlinear dynamics vary smoothly with an observable transition variable.
description: Blend autoregressive regimes continuously with a logistic or exponential transition function.
failure_conditions: Limited observations near the transition region make slope and threshold estimates unstable.

assumptions: Transformed seasonal dynamics and residual autocorrelation remain stable.
description: Combine Box-Cox transformation, ARMA errors, trend, and one seasonal component in state space.
failure_conditions: Multiple or rapidly changing seasonalities are not captured by a single seasonal state.

assumptions: Complex seasonalities can be represented by stable Fourier state components.
description: Extend BATS with trigonometric states so multiple and non-integer seasonal periods can be modeled.
failure_conditions: Long histories and many harmonics make fitting expensive and can overfit weak cycles.

assumptions: Seasonal shapes are smooth and repeat while residual autocorrelation follows ARIMA dynamics.
description: Regress on Fourier terms for one or more seasonal periods while modeling remaining errors with ARIMA.
failure_conditions: Changing seasonal timing or event-driven pulses cannot be represented by fixed harmonics.

assumptions: Several stable seasonal periods coexist and can be separated additively.
description: Decompose multiple seasonal periods with repeated STL, forecast the adjusted series with ETS, and restore each seasonal component.
failure_conditions: Short histories or interacting seasonal amplitudes make the sequential decomposition unreliable.

assumptions: Historical feature-target relationships recur within the range covered by training data.
description: Train an ensemble of randomized regression trees on lag, rolling, calendar, and optional exogenous features.
failure_conditions: Trees do not extrapolate trends beyond observed target regions and recursive forecasts compound errors.

assumptions: Engineered features expose repeatable nonlinear splits predictive of future targets.
description: Boost regularized regression trees over lag, rolling, calendar, and exogenous features.
failure_conditions: Extrapolation and unseen regimes remain weak even when in-range fit is strong.

assumptions: Large enough supervised windows support stable nonlinear partitions of engineered features.
description: Fit histogram-based leaf-wise gradient-boosted trees to time-series lag and covariate features.
failure_conditions: Leaf-wise growth overfits small series and cannot reliably extrapolate outside training targets.

assumptions: Pretraining patterns transfer to the target frequency and forecast horizon.
description: A patched decoder-only transformer pretrained across heterogeneous series for direct point forecasting.
failure_conditions: Large domain shifts or required context beyond the checkpoint limit reduce zero-shot reliability.

assumptions: Quantized sequence patterns learned from public and synthetic corpora transfer to the target.
description: Scale and quantize values into tokens, then sample continuations from a pretrained T5 language-model family.
failure_conditions: Quantization, unmodeled covariates, and autoregressive sampling can miss sharp conditional events.

assumptions: Cross-frequency and cross-variate patterns in LOTSA transfer to the target variables.
description: A masked encoder universal forecaster using multi-patch-size projections and an any-variate attention design.
failure_conditions: Unseen covariate semantics or data distributions can defeat the universal patch representation.

assumptions: Lag covariates provide a frequency-robust representation transferable across domains.
description: A decoder-only probabilistic forecaster that conditions on lagged values and time features across frequencies.
failure_conditions: Long nonseasonal dependencies and unseen exogenous shocks are poorly represented by fixed lag features.

assumptions: Pretrained representations can be adapted with a small amount of task supervision.
description: A masked-patch encoder pretrained on the Time-series Pile and adapted with task-specific forecasting heads.
failure_conditions: A fixed patch context and weak target-specific adaptation can miss long-horizon dynamics.

assumptions: Resolution-diverse pretraining transfers and a small adaptation head captures target specifics.
description: A compact adaptive-patching mixer pretrained for zero-shot use and lightweight target or covariate adaptation.
failure_conditions: Checkpoint-specific context and horizon pairs constrain direct use on mismatched tasks.

assumptions: Next-patch generative pretraining learns patterns reusable under the target sampling process.
description: A GPT-style model pretrained by next-patch prediction and adapted to forecasting and other generative time-series tasks.
failure_conditions: Channel-independent generation and finite context can miss new cross-variate causal structure.

assumptions: Sparse experts specialize in reusable temporal regimes across large heterogeneous pretraining data.
description: A sparse mixture-of-experts decoder pretrained autoregressively on the Time-300B corpus.
failure_conditions: Unsupported dynamic covariates and context-plus-horizon beyond the trained window limit applicability.

assumptions: The synthetic prior assigns meaningful probability to the target data-generating behavior.
description: A prior-data-fitted network trained on synthetic generators to approximate Bayesian zero-shot forecasting.
failure_conditions: Real dynamics outside the synthetic training prior lead to systematic zero-shot errors.

assumptions: The proprietary pretraining corpus and service adaptation transfer to the submitted target.
description: A hosted pretrained forecasting service supporting zero-shot forecasts, intervals, and exogenous inputs.
failure_conditions: Closed weights and training data limit diagnosis under domain shift or service changes.

assumptions: Prompt and decomposition components align the target distribution with pretrained regimes.
description: A prompt-conditioned pretrained transformer that decomposes trend, seasonality, and residual structure for transfer.
failure_conditions: Incorrect decomposition or a target outside prompt coverage produces negative transfer.

assumptions: A shared sequence-variable representation transfers across tasks and domains with prompting or adaptation.
description: A unified task-tokenized time-series model that supports forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly detection.
failure_conditions: Task and domain shifts not represented during pretraining require substantial target-specific tuning.

assumptions: Flow-matching pretraining on TimeBench captures a transferable conditional future distribution.
description: A native continuous-value transformer trained with flow matching to generate multiple future paths.
failure_conditions: Unseen domains or event-conditioned futures absent from numeric context remain underrepresented.

assumptions: Large observability and synthetic pretraining transfers to the target variables and covariates.
description: A multivariate decoder-only probabilistic forecaster scaled for observability and general forecasting data.
failure_conditions: Targets far from observability dynamics or hardware limits for larger checkpoints reduce usefulness.

assumptions: At least half of the component forecasts remain reasonably centered.
description: Take the pointwise median of forecasts from heterogeneous component methods.
failure_conditions: A majority of similarly biased components moves the median in the wrong direction.

assumptions: Recent relative validation performance persists into the forecast window.
description: Weight component forecasts inversely to their rolling-origin validation errors.
failure_conditions: Noisy short validation windows assign extreme weight to accidental winners.

assumptions: The estimated error covariance is stable and component forecasts are approximately unbiased.
description: Estimate component error covariance and choose minimum-variance linear combination weights.
failure_conditions: Ill-conditioned covariance estimates produce unstable or extreme weights.

assumptions: Out-of-fold component error relationships transfer to the future window.
description: Train a second-level regressor on out-of-fold component forecasts to produce the final forecast.
failure_conditions: Leakage or too few folds causes the meta-regressor to overfit component noise.

assumptions: Component quantiles share the same probability levels and are individually ordered.
description: Average corresponding predictive quantiles from multiple probabilistic forecasters.
failure_conditions: Miscalibrated or dependent components can preserve bias and yield incoherent quantile curves.

assumptions: Historical forecast-origin errors rank candidate methods similarly to the next origin.
description: Select the single component with the lowest rolling-origin validation loss for the target horizon.
failure_conditions: A regime change after the last validation origin makes the historical champion obsolete.

assumptions: A representative reference collection links series features to relative model performance.
description: Map time-series features to learned nonnegative weights over a pool of forecasting methods.
failure_conditions: Targets outside the reference feature distribution receive unreliable weights.

assumptions: Enough historical origins exist to estimate horizon-specific error rankings.
description: Choose a potentially different validated component for each forecast horizon step.
failure_conditions: Sparse long-horizon validation creates a jagged and unstable sequence of selections.

assumptions: Observable history features identify which expert is reliable for each target.
description: Use a learned gating model to assign target-dependent weights to statistical and foundation forecasters.
failure_conditions: The gate overfits a small task collection or ignores a new failure mode shared by all experts.

assumptions: The series contains separable linear and nonlinear components.
description: Forecast a linear ARIMA component and add a neural forecast fitted to its residual structure.
failure_conditions: Residual dependence changes after fitting or both components model the same signal twice.

assumptions: Systematic residual autocorrelation remains after the foundation forecast.
description: Use TimesFM as the primary path and add an ARIMA forecast of historical primary-model residuals.
failure_conditions: Residuals estimated from too few pseudo-origins are noisy or change regime at deployment.

assumptions: Residual bias is predictable from historical, calendar, or known-future features.
description: Add a lag-feature gradient-boosting correction trained on pseudo-out-of-sample Chronos residuals.
failure_conditions: In-sample residual leakage or unseen covariate states causes an oversized correction.

assumptions: ETS captures structural components while remaining residual dependence is linear and stable.
description: Forecast level, trend, and seasonality with ETS, then add an autoregressive residual forecast.
failure_conditions: Residual correction double-counts seasonal dynamics or amplifies a structural break.

assumptions: History-only validation can detect harmful foundation-model mismatch before deployment.
description: Use a foundation forecast only when it clears a margin over a statistical challenger in rolling validation.
failure_conditions: A future event changes the regime in a way no historical fold can reveal.

assumptions: Pretraining is more reliable than local estimation only in the short-history regime.
description: Use a zero-shot foundation model below a data threshold and switch to a fitted statistical model once history is sufficient.
failure_conditions: The threshold is poorly calibrated or the foundation model is mismatched to the target domain.

assumptions: The anomaly diagnostic separates contamination from genuine persistent changes.
description: Choose a robust or intervention-adjusted forecaster when anomaly diagnostics exceed a threshold, otherwise use the primary model.
failure_conditions: A true regime shift is labeled as an outlier and routed to an inappropriate robust fallback.

assumptions: Fallback parents are valid substitutes and operational failures are detected before emitting a forecast.
description: Execute an ordered list of forecasters and fall back when a model cannot satisfy context, covariate, device, or runtime constraints.
failure_conditions: Silent model degradation passes the availability checks and prevents fallback activation.
